semantic_correction.stem: Soon after a vaginal birth and placental delivery, a client has heavy vaginal bleeding. The uterus is soft, boggy, and midline. Which action should the nurse take?

options.A: Begin uterine massage and activate the facility's postpartum-hemorrhage response while continuing rapid assessment.
options.B: Delay intervention until the blood loss is formally quantified, then decide whether postpartum-hemorrhage treatment is needed.
options.C: Inspect for a laceration first and postpone uterine massage until trauma has been excluded as the bleeding source.
options.D: Have the client attempt to void first, then reassess the uterine tone before activating the postpartum-hemorrhage response.

semantic_correction.rationale: The 2025 WHO consolidated guideline for postpartum haemorrhage identifies uterine atony as a common cause of PPH and states that a soft or boggy uterus should prompt immediate clinical response. WHO recommends uterine massage for treatment of PPH and places it within a rapid first-response treatment bundle that also includes uterotonics, tranexamic acid, intravenous fluids, examination for the bleeding source, and escalation of care. The stem supplies heavy bleeding plus a soft, boggy, midline uterus, making uterine atony the immediate high-priority finding. The nurse should begin uterine massage and activate the facility's PPH response while continuing rapid assessment rather than waiting for formal quantification, postponing uterine-tone treatment until lacerations are excluded, or delaying the hemorrhage response for voiding. The 2026 NCSBN NCLEX-RN Test Plan explicitly includes care for clients experiencing pregnancy/labor/delivery complications such as hemorrhage. Therefore A is the uniquely best answer.
semantic_correction.educational_objective: Recognize heavy postpartum bleeding with a soft boggy uterus as a uterine-atony emergency requiring immediate uterine massage and activation of the postpartum-hemorrhage response while evaluation and treatment proceed rapidly.
semantic_correction.source_organization: World Health Organization (WHO), via NCBI Bookshelf; National Council of State Boards of Nursing (NCSBN)
semantic_correction.source_document_title: Consolidated guidelines for the prevention, diagnosis and treatment of postpartum haemorrhage; 2026 NCLEX-RN Test Plan
semantic_correction.source_version_date: WHO consolidated postpartum haemorrhage guideline 2025; NCSBN Test Plan published 2025 and effective April 1, 2026 through March 31, 2029
semantic_correction.source_locator: WHO consolidated PPH guideline > Recommendations and supporting evidence > uterine tone assessment — soft/boggy uterus should prompt further examination and clinical response; First-response treatment of postpartum haemorrhage > Recommendation 26 — uterine massage recommended for treatment of PPH and included in rapid first-response treatment bundle. NCSBN 2026 NCLEX-RN Test Plan > Physiological Adaptation > Alterations in Body Systems, printed p. 47 / PDF p. 51 — provide care for client experiencing complications of pregnancy/labor and/or delivery including hemorrhage.
semantic_correction.source_claim_supported: A soft boggy postpartum uterus with heavy bleeding warrants immediate clinical response; uterine massage is recommended as part of rapid first-response treatment for postpartum hemorrhage caused by uterine atony.

semantic_correction.correction_summary_append: RULE1 cleanup: retired an FMEA terminology item because it tested quality-improvement vocabulary rather than entry-level bedside nursing and duplicated an existing QI-tool cluster. Rebuilt this UID into recognition and immediate response to postpartum hemorrhage with a soft boggy uterus.

audit_findings_append.finding: The replacement tests a direct maternal emergency action. WHO supports immediate response to a boggy uterus and recommends uterine massage as part of first-response PPH treatment; NCSBN explicitly includes hemorrhage among pregnancy/labor/delivery complications.
audit_findings_append.source_authority: WHO 2025 consolidated PPH guideline; NCSBN 2026 NCLEX-RN Test Plan
audit_findings_append.source_locator: WHO uterine-tone assessment and Recommendation 26; NCSBN Physiological Adaptation printed p. 47 / PDF p. 51

scope_exclusions.blood_loss_threshold: No numerical blood-loss threshold is used to diagnose PPH in the item. The stem provides clinically significant heavy bleeding plus uterine atony and asks for immediate nursing response.
scope_exclusions.uterotonic_choice: No specific uterotonic medication, dose, contraindication, or sequence is prescribed; the facility PPH response determines medication treatment.
scope_exclusions.tranexamic_acid_timing: No TXA dose or treatment window is tested.
scope_exclusions.bladder_distention: The uterus is explicitly midline, reducing the likelihood that bladder displacement is the primary explanation; voiding may be useful in some cases but should not delay the hemorrhage response in this scenario.

near_duplicate_check.note: Targeted GitHub search for 'postpartum boggy uterus heavy bleeding fundal massage' returned no indexed repository match. No broad bank rescan was performed.

option_audit.A: Correct. It addresses the boggy uterus immediately and activates the broader hemorrhage response while assessment and treatment continue.
option_audit.B: Plausible because blood-loss measurement is important, but treatment should not be delayed until quantification is complete when heavy bleeding and uterine atony are already present.
option_audit.C: Plausible because trauma is another cause of PPH, but the soft boggy uterus requires immediate treatment rather than postponing uterine massage while lacerations are excluded.
option_audit.D: Plausible because bladder emptying can improve uterine tone when distention is contributing, but the uterus is midline and the active hemorrhage response should not be delayed.

ambiguity_check: No second defensible best answer. A addresses the source-supported atony pattern immediately and triggers the broader PPH response. B, C and D each delay treatment despite heavy bleeding and a soft boggy uterus.

cueing_check.note: Exact character counts were calculated from the stored strings. The correct answer is not longest and all four choices are realistic postpartum-management actions.

blueprint_audit.entry_level_relevance: NCSBN explicitly includes caring for a client experiencing complications of pregnancy/labor/delivery, including hemorrhage, under Physiological Adaptation. Immediate recognition and escalation of uterine atony is directly relevant to entry-level RN practice.
blueprint_audit.visual_verification: PASS. Official NCSBN 2026 Test Plan printed p. 47 / PDF p. 51 was visually inspected on 2026-08-20 and visibly lists care for pregnancy/labor/delivery complications including hemorrhage.
